# Protocol Decodings & Specifications: New Aether HE Boards

*Generated by Fable-5 (MiniMax-M3) — Deep Protocol Analysis*

This document synthesizes the protocol layer, HID descriptors, and command byte structures for the newly logged Aether keyboards (Aula F75, Aula Mini 60 HE Pro, Win60 He Max, win68 HE Max, WIN 60 HE Pro). The analysis is derived from user-provided GitHub issues, hardware metrics, and pre-existing protocol heuristics within the `aether-windows` ecosystem.

---

## 1. Aula Mini 60 HE Pro
* **VID:PID:** `0C45:80A2` (wired) · `0C45:FEFE` (2.4GHz dongle)
* **Form Factor:** 60% Magnetic
* **Controller Family:** Sonix (from the `0C45` prefix)

> **⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-07-20 — tested on hardware.** This section previously stated the board
> was *"guaranteed to utilize the Sonix 0xAA-framed vendor protocol"* because it shares VID
> `0C45` with the decoded `0C45:80A1`. **That inference was tested against the physical board
> and falsified.** The text below it (the `0xAA` framing, cmd `0x23`/`0x27` layouts) is an
> accurate description of the **`80A1` Max** protocol, but it is NOT confirmed for this board —
> treat it as a hypothesis to check a capture against, not as this board's spec. The original
> "guaranteed" claim was inference presented as fact; it survived because nobody had the
> hardware. Now we do.

### Measured HID topology (hardware, 2026-07-20)
The board enumerates as **two different devices** depending on transport:

| Transport | VID:PID | Product string | Vendor interfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| USB-C cable | `0C45:80A2` | `KEYBOARD  MINI 60 HE PRO` | iface 2 `0xFF68`/`0x61`; iface 3 `0xFF67`/`0x61` |
| 2.4GHz dongle | `0C45:FEFE` | `MINI 60 HE PRO Dongle` | iface 2 `0xFFFF`/`0x01`; iface 3 `0xFF60`/`0x61`; iface 4 `0xFF59`/`0x61` |

Note the dongle exposes **no `0xFF68` at all** — the two transports do not present the same
vendor surface, so a wired decode will not automatically yield the wireless one.
`0xFF60`/`0x61` on the dongle is the canonical **QMK/VIA raw-HID** signature and is worth
pulling as an independent lead.

### Falsification test (wired, `80A2`, iface 2 `0xFF68`)
The Max's decoded lighting command was driven directly at the board:

* Every `protocol_sonix` cmd `0x23` frame is **accepted** by hidapi (65 bytes written, no error).
* The board **echoes the frame back verbatim with magic `0x55` replacing the request `0xAA`**.
* **No LED change**, across the full mode sweep `0x00..0x11` at brightness `0xFF`.
* The echo is byte-identical to what was sent — **not one field clamped or normalized**, even
  for nonsense mode values. Firmware that genuinely parsed the mode byte would be expected to
  normalize at least one invalid value. This reads as a **dumb loopback, not a semantic ACK**.
* iface 3 (`0xFF67`) rejects writes outright (`write()` returns `-1`).

**Conclusion:** same-usage-page is no stronger evidence than same-VID was. `80A2` is
`protocol: null` in the registry and stays there until it has its **own** USBPcap capture of the
official Aula driver. Reproduce with the probe methodology in
`docs/context/aula-win60-protocol-capture.md`.

### Exact Command Structures (0C45 Family)
Frames are constructed *without* a standard HID Report ID. Instead, every 64-byte frame starts with a magic header:
`[0]=0xAA [1]=CMD [2]=LENGTH [3]=OFFSET_LO [4]=OFFSET_HI`

**Lighting Command (`CMD 0x23`):**
Controls global RGB settings.
* `[6]` = `0x01` (Fixed flag)
* `[8]` = Lighting Mode (e.g., `0x02` for Static)
* `[9]` = Red (0-255)
* `[10]` = Green (0-255)
* `[11]` = Blue (0-255)
* `[12]` = Alpha/Global Brightness modifier
* `[16]` = Sub-flag (Animation direction/modifier)
* `[17]` = Brightness Level
* `[18]` = Animation Speed
* `[22..23]` = `0xAA 0x55` (Termination marker)

**Actuation & Rapid Trigger Command (`CMD 0x27`):**
Controls per-key HE magnetic switch thresholds, paged in 56-byte (`0x38`) payloads to fit within the 64-byte frame limit.
* Records are packed contiguously from byte `[9]`.
* **8-Byte Record Structure (Per Key):**
  * `[0]` = Enable Flag (`0x00` = Off, `0x01` = On)
  * `[1]` = Trigger Mode (`0xAA` = Fixed Actuation, `0x43` = Rapid Trigger)
  * `[2..3]` = Press Threshold (16-bit **Big-Endian**, in `0.01 mm` units)
  * `[4..5]` = Release Threshold (16-bit **Big-Endian**, in `0.01 mm` units)
  * `[6..7]` = Padding (`0x00 0x00`)
* *Note: Cross-frame table alignment requires verification on `FEFE` silicon.*

## 2. Aula WIN 60 HE Pro
* **VID:PID:** `8089:0009`
* **Form Factor:** 60% Magnetic
* **Hardware:** `CH32V307RBT6` MCU (32KB SRAM, 128KB Flash) on PCB rev `SI-2825C-CH32-USB-V1.1`
* **Controller Family:** SayoDevice

### Protocol Assessment & HID Structures
This board is marketed under the "Aula Win60 HE" umbrella but operates on a completely different silicon stack. It flashes and runs custom-ported **SayoDevice base firmware** (`base_SI_2825C_CH32_USB_V1_1.bin`), achieving a 4.7KHz scan rate via x4 oversampling. 

* **Usage Page Configurations:** 
  It utilizes three distinct vendor collections on Interface 1, matching standard SayoDevice descriptors:
  * `Usage Page 0xFF00, Usage 0x01` (Primary Config)
  * `Usage Page 0xFF11, Usage 0x02`
  * `Usage Page 0xFF12, Usage 0x02`

### Exact Command Structures
Because it runs SayoDevice firmware, it ignores Aula's WebHID standard (`CMD 33`, `CMD 7`, etc.). Deep decoding of the SayoDevice protocol is required to drive it natively:
* **Actuation/Lighting:** Must adhere to SayoDevice's memory-mapped read/write specifications (often utilizing 64-byte chunks starting with specific opcodes for memory offsets).
* *Actionable Step:* An integration with the `sayo-device` open-source protocol libraries (or a raw dump from `sayodevice.com`) is mandatory to establish the payload mappings for this specific CH32 MCU target.

## 3. Aula Win60 HE Max & win68 HE Max
* **VID:PID:** `1CA2:1902` (60%) & `1CA2:1901` (65%)
* **Controller Family:** WINxxHE MAX (Wired, ~500mA)

### Protocol Assessment & HID Structures
Despite sharing the "Win60 HE" naming convention, the `1CA2` VID denotes a third distinct OEM controller family. 
* **Capabilities:** Supports "True Analog Gamepad Emulation", interfacing via `magnet.aulastar.com` (and `hub.aulacn.com`).
* **Protocol Void:** Currently, no HID dumps, usage pages, or protocol captures exist for `1CA2` boards. 
* *Actionable Step:* They are strictly untestable until a USBPcap trace of the lighting and actuation writes is supplied. They are highly unlikely to use the standard `2E3C` (Aula) or `0C45` (Sonix) transport framing.

## 4. Aula F75 Tri-Mode
* **VID:PID:** `258A:010C`
* **Form Factor:** 75% Mechanical (Standard digital switches)
* **Controller Family:** Standard Aula (Standalone Desktop Driver)

### Protocol Assessment & HID Structures
This is a standard mechanical keyboard utilizing traditional digital switches. 
* **Protocol Void:** It lacks magnetic Hall-Effect sensors, meaning `CMD 0x27` (Rapid Trigger) and `CMD 0x33` (Analog Travel) paradigms do not apply. 
* *Actionable Step:* Decoding will center strictly on keymap overrides and RGB lighting effects. Requires a USBPcap capture of the `AULA_F75_Setup_v2.0` standalone driver payload to identify its `Usage Page` and command frames.
